theory.say:
• You own the file's movement; Atty. Thorne owns every legal judgment
• Case Management: the end-to-end coordination, tracking and handling of a case, from intake to resolution
• It ensures three things: timely progression, proper documentation and compliance, effective communication between all parties
• First duties: case updates and summaries Atty. Thorne can decide from in one read
• Research the relevant laws and rules, and draft and file every document to the firm's standard

theory2.say:
• Watch task compliance and case progress: every task owned and dated, every phase moving
• Client communication: John Doe kept informed, every contact logged the same day
• Case health analysis: read the whole file for risk, like a missed deadline, a silent client or a gap in treatment
• Allocate resources and recommend next steps; strategy itself stays with Atty. Thorne

frame.say:
• The General Process runs in seven steps, from intake and case opening to resolution and closing
• Intake includes the Conflict Check; planning means you draft, Atty. Thorne sets strategy
• Documentation and communication: the CMS is the single source of truth, every contact logged
• Monitoring: every deadline docketed; billing support keeps bills, liens and costs current for the demand
• Each case phase, Intake to Litigation, has its own goals, responsibilities and deliverables

rules.say:
• Case Manager owns deadlines, documents, insurers, doctors and client updates
• Atty. Thorne owns every legal judgment: value, strength, strategy, whether to settle
• Log every contact, document and deadline in the CMS the same day; if it isn't in the CMS, it didn't happen
• Allowed: explain the process, confirm facts; never: tell a client the case value or whether to take an offer
• Red flag: a note to Atty. Thorne headed "Update": the ask waits, the SOL, 02/06/2028, doesn't; rewrite it as the decision and its deadline

model.say:

• Liens: bills paid out of the settlement before the client gets their share
• Litigation is dashed: the path only taken if the case doesn't settle
• Navy band: Case Manager owns the movement; orange band: Atty. Thorne owns every legal judgment
• The CMS sits under station one because the whole track runs on it

map.say:

• 1 Conflict Check: every party's full legal name, before the file exists; 2 verify date of loss against the Police Report
• 3 Calendar the statute of limitations, the legal deadline to sue, on day one
• 4 Map every role and client seating; 5 insurance from the Dec Page; 6 name and file every document

theory.say:

• Your role: verify and organize the essential facts while making sure the case meets acceptance standards
• Initial client contact gathers the basic facts, assesses urgency and decides whether the case can move forward

theory2.say:

• Review every document for completeness and relevance; name the file and enter it in the system properly
• Work independently: spot missing or inconsistent information, decide on basic acceptance, and tell the client or team the next steps

theory.say:
• The Case Plan is the file's instruction manual; Atty. Thorne sets strategy from it, and a hidden risk builds it on a false picture
• Example: John Doe's 14-day Treatment Gap belongs in the plan; opinions about him or case value do not
• Early evaluation answers three questions: is there money, who is responsible, how will the case move
• Coverage determination: which policies apply, their benefits, limits and exclusions; liability assessment: who caused the crash, clear, shared or disputed, on what evidence
• Case projection: early read on risk and direction; case value always stays with the attorney
• Strict compliance: every plan deadline goes on the calendar

frame.say:
• Coverage: is there money? Valid policies, coverage type, limits, exclusions, gaps
• Liability: who is responsible and how much? Includes comparative negligence: the client sharing some blame
• Projection: how will the case move? Draws on coverage, liability, injury, expected treatment, paperwork quality
• Projection comes last because it depends on the other two

rules.say:

• Projection stays preliminary until coverage is confirmed; liability needs the Police Report, statements, any video
• Hold a place for the Regulatory Triple-Check, cleared in the Treatment Phase
• File the plan within the state's window, often 30 to 60 days, and calendar it
• Every goal gets a measure, owner, date; flag bad facts loudly; value is Atty. Thorne's

theory.say:
• No such thing as full coverage: every policy pays a different thing; ask whose it is and what it pays
• Two separate questions: who pays the bills now, who pays the claim later
• Payer-First Principle: each bill goes to the payer that must pay it first, or it returns as a lien on John Doe's settlement
• Third-party coverage is the at-fault driver's, Robert Smith's; first-party is the client's side, and UM follows the person: John Doe has no car policy
• Recovery Stack: only coverage that pays the claim: BI (bodily injury on the at-fault driver), then UM/UIM
• MedPay and PIP: no-fault medical coverage paying accident bills fast, regardless of fault

theory2.say:
• Set-off and non-duplication: some policies subtract what PIP or MedPay paid; verify in writing
• Subrogation: a payer's right to be repaid from the settlement
• Contract rate and write-off: in-network providers accept the Health Plan's price, so the lien is smaller
• Medicare Secondary Payer: Medicare pays last, is repaid by law, case reported to the BCRC
• Bill first the payer with no right to be repaid
• Claim numbers: Keystone KM-26-440871, Harbor Point HP-26-7741, Cardinal State CS-26-20355

frame.say:
• BI liability: at-fault driver's, third-party, pays the injury claim
• UM/UIM: client's side, through vehicle or household, pays when BI is too small; consent rules apply
• PIP: from the vehicle the client rode in, pays Medical Bills without proving fault; verify repayment terms in writing
• Health insurance: client's plan, contract rate, right to be repaid
• Medicare and Medicaid: last, repaid by law, BCRC report

rules.say:

• Post each payment on its ledger

theory.say:
• Adjusters, IME doctors (examiners the insurer hires) and defense lawyers compare John Doe's records to a standard map of recovery

• Standard Treatment Map: ambulance and ER, imaging, chiropractic and therapy, orthopedics and pain management, surgery only if serious
• A skipped or out-of-order stop needs a medical reason on file
• Clinical Pathway: is he improving? If not, variance loop, figuring out why; next steps are the doctor's decision

theory2.say:

• Red Flag Rule: no disability score change after 12 weeks is a plateau; specialist or second opinion is the doctor's call
• Objective metrics: Oswestry or DASH every 30 days, walking test, PHQ-9 and GAD-7 when stalled, FCE before return to work
• Stakeholder Triad: clinic, lawyer and insurer, with the Case Manager passing information

frame.say:

• Sub-acute, weeks 2 to 8: active therapy two or three times a week, specialists; watch range-of-motion gains
• Restorative, weeks 9 to 24: work hardening, injections, emotional support; look for return-to-work blockers
• Maintenance, six months on: home exercises; question is MMI, Maximum Medical Improvement
• Discharge, maybe an impairment rating; every treatment is a doctor's order, never ours

• Don't: argue with resistance or warn that missed visits hurt his case
• Don't: report a yellow flag with no plan or follow-up date, or treat late head-injury symptoms as proof
• The Case Manager listens and engages; never decides tests, medications or referrals
dodont.ask: Which yellow flag might show up for John Doe, and what open question would uncover it?

why.say:
• PIP: the client's own insurance paying Medical Bills regardless of fault, written state by state
• Florida's Emergency Medical Condition (EMC) rule decides early whether PIP pays $2,500, $10,000, or no medical
• John Doe's file is in Riverton: add-on PIP, no EMC rule, so Harbor Point's $5,000 PIP isn't capped
• On a Florida file, the clock starts at the date of loss; the Case Manager calendars it
• Had this file been in Florida, day 14 was 02/20/2026, his first treatment
• Red flag: telling a Riverton client his PIP is capped over the 14 days; Riverton has no EMC rule

rules.say:
• Florida PIP, Fla. Stat. 627.736, always confirm the current statute: $10,000, paying 80% of reasonable medical and 60% of lost income
• Initial care within 14 days or PIP pays no medical: calendar day 14 at intake; tell the client the deadline and where care is available
• Full $10,000 only if an MD, DO, dentist, PA or APRN finds an EMC, else $2,500; chiropractors can't; log each provider's credential
• EMC: going without care could seriously harm health; check the first record's date, provider and written EMC, request it if missing
• Track the bucket in the PIP Log; a missing EMC or late first visit goes to Atty. Thorne that day
